title: Mandhana tops women's T20I run charts as India crush Bangladesh to reach Asian Games final
excerpt: Smriti Mandhana passed Suzie Bates with a 19-ball 37 in the Asian Games semifinal, while Shafali Verma's unbeaten 49-ball century powered India to a 114-run win and a gold-medal clash with Sri Lanka.
body:
• Smriti Mandhana passed New Zealand's Suzie Bates to become the highest run-scorer in women's T20I history during India's Asian Games semifinal against Bangladesh on Sunday.
  • Mandhana needed eight runs to break Bates's mark of 4,758; she reached the milestone with back-to-back fours and finished with 37 off 19 balls, taking her tally to 4,788.
  • Shafali Verma smashed an unbeaten 100 off 49 balls — the first century in Asian Games women's cricket — as India posted 195/4 and beat Bangladesh by 114 runs.
  • Defending champions India will face Sri Lanka, who beat Pakistan by eight wickets, in the gold-medal match at Korogi Sports Park.

Smriti Mandhana became the leading run-scorer in women's T20 international history on Sunday, passing Suzie Bates during India's crushing 114-run win over Bangladesh in the Asian Games semifinal in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.

The India opener came into the game at Korogi Sports Park with 4,751 T20I runs — eight short of Bates's 4,758. She got there in style, hitting back-to-back fours off Marufa Akter's third over before finishing with a 19-ball 37, decorated with five fours and two sixes. Her tally now stands at 4,788 runs in 171 innings.

ICC chairman Jay Shah led the congratulations, writing on X: "Many congratulations to @mandhana_smriti for going top of the Women's T20I run charts (4,788 runs). By rewriting history, you are lifting women's cricket to new heights and setting the standard for young dreamers everywhere."

Shafali's hundred steals the show

Mandhana's milestone shared the spotlight with a remarkable innings from Shafali Verma, whose unbeaten 100 off 49 balls was the first century in Asian Games women's cricket history. The 22-year-old opener hit three fours and nine sixes at a strike rate of 204.08, reaching her hundred only in the final over of India's innings.

"ICC chairman Jay Shah led the congratulations, writing on X: "Many congratulations to @mandhana_smriti for going top of the Women's T20I run charts (4,788 runs)."

Shafali also broke Mandhana's own record for the most sixes by an Indian in women's T20I cricket — a record swapping hands within the same innings.

The openers raced to 72 for the first wicket inside the powerplay before Mandhana fell, caught behind off Nahida Akter attempting a slog sweep. Shafali then added 94 off 55 balls with captain Harmanpreet Kaur (40 off 33) as India closed on 195/4.

Bangladesh never got going in reply, bowled out for 81. The margin — 114 runs — underscored the gulf between the defending champions and the rest of the field.

Context & Background

The record is the latest in a rich seam of landmarks for Mandhana. Earlier this month, she passed Mithali Raj to become the highest run-scorer in women's international cricket overall, scoring 124 off 64 against Hong Kong in the Women's Asia Cup 2026 in Dubai. She now leads the all-time women's T20I list ahead of Bates (4,758), Harmanpreet Kaur (4,287), Sri Lanka's Chamari Athapaththu (4,282) and New Zealand's Sophie Devine (3,817).

India are the defending Asian Games women's cricket champions and have treated the tournament as a statement of dominance ahead of a busy season. The final against Sri Lanka — who defeated Pakistan by eight wickets in the first semifinal — sets up a clash of the two form teams of the competition.

Impact & Analysis

Mandhana's record is not just a numbers milestone; it reflects longevity at the top of a format she has helped redefine. Since her T20I debut in 2013, she has scored two centuries and 36 half-centuries while carrying India's batting through four World Cup cycles. Holding the T20I run record simultaneously with the all-international mark makes her, statistically, the most prolific batter women's cricket has produced.

Sunday's performance also answered the composure question: she reached the record in 19 balls of pure intent rather than a nervous crawl — 37 runs at a strike rate of 194.7, in a semifinal, with the milestone looming.

Diaspora Angle

Mandhana's records travel. Diaspora families in the US, UK and Canada will find her at the top of every all-time chart their kids will Google first — a readymade role model at a time when women's cricket is still fighting for visibility abroad.

What's Next

India face Sri Lanka in the gold-medal match with a title and an undefeated tournament run on the line. Mandhana will have a chance to stretch her new record further — and Sri Lanka's Athapaththu, fourth on the all-time list, will be trying to close the gap from the other end.
